advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the wrapper's scanner threshold cannot silently drift from 15 (e.g. pass the same --config used by the tests/runbook, or assert the resolved mccabe setting) so pyproject removal/change is caught rather than silently altering the gate.
evidence: docstring/tests use "--config", "lint.mccabe.max-complexity=15" (test_complexity_baseline.py _live_census) but the production scanner omits it
COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD = 15 is defined but only used for baseline ceiling validation, not for asserting the scanner's effective threshold
advisory.finding: run_scanner's RUFF_SCAN_ARGS does not pass '--config lint.mccabe.max-complexity=15' and relies solely on pyproject.toml discovery, whereas the tests and runbook invoke Ruff with the explicit --config. Nothing in the scanner path asserts the effective threshold is 15, so if the [tool.ruff.lint.mccabe] entry were removed or changed, the gate would silently scan at a different threshold than its documented contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fixture with two functions on one physical line (distinct name columns) asserting both correct column-disambiguated resolution and the ambiguous-line NormalizationError.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:180-182 `keyword_len = 10 if isinstance(child, ast.AsyncFunctionDef) else 4` / `name_col = child.col_offset + keyword_len + 1`

scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:203-206 `exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]` ... `raise NormalizationError(f"ambiguous function definition at line {row}, column {column}")`

test_resolve_nested_equal_leaf_under_different_parents / test_resolve_async_and_nested / test_resolve_lambda_location_has_no_symbol all call resolve_symbol with column 0 and SYMBOL_SRC has no two defs sharing a line

ABSENCE: no test constructs a source with two `def`s on the same line + distinct name columns to drive either the len(exact)==1 happy path or the ambiguous-failure branch; `search_files` for 'column' in the test file returned no matches
advisory.finding: The column-based symbol disambiguation logic (build_symbol_index name-column computation and resolve_symbol's exact-column match / ambiguous-line NormalizationError) is never exercised: every fixture places one function per line and passes column 0/1, so resolution always short-circuits on len(candidates)==1 before the column code runs. A regression in keyword_len (4 vs 10) or the column comparison would pass all tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests over a source like `def a(): ...; def b(): ...` (or a compound line) that assert resolve_symbol returns the correct qualified name when column matches one candidate, and raises NormalizationError('ambiguous...') when the column matches none/both.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the name_col heuristic (col_offset + keyword_len + 1) is robust to non-single-space formatting, or derive the name column from the AST/token stream rather than assuming one space.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:180: keyword_len = 10 if isinstance(child, ast.AsyncFunctionDef) else 4
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:203: exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]
Only reached when >1 function definition shares a line (single-candidate lines return candidates[0][1] without using column); ruff format normalizes spacing so this is unlikely in practice.
dropped.finding: build_symbol_index computes the function-name column as col_offset + keyword_len + 1, assuming exactly one whitespace character between the def/async def keyword and the function name. Extra spaces (e.g. 'def  foo') would produce a wrong name_col and could break the multiple-defs-on-one-line disambiguation in resolve_symbol.

evidence: docs note: `Resolve the project's pinned Ruff first (do not assume a version)` — implying a pin is expected, but no pin appears in the pyproject.toml hunk
The pyproject.toml diff only touches `[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]` and `per-file-ignores`, not `[project.dependencies]` or a dev/lint dependency group
dropped.finding: The gate's correctness depends on the resolved `ruff` executable version (McCabe scoring can change across Ruff releases), but the diff does not show `ruff` pinned in the dependency manifest; an unpinned or drifting Ruff could silently change C901 scores and invalidate the committed baseline.
